sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h1 variant (nation-rate editions) joined to Doc 2's Annex 1 Table 7: a filter fixed by two editions (which nations fell from 2021 to 2022), then the highest individual agreement among them. Medium target (no Easy slot); measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 3 L68-76 (2021) and Doc 1 L42-50 (2022) give the changes: England -0.3, Scotland -0.9 (fell); Wales 0; Northern Ireland +0.2 (rose). Doc 2 L1454-1460 Table 7 Agree (individuals): England 61.6, Wales 51.4, Scotland 65.5, NI 79.0, UK 62.5. Highest among England and Scotland: 65.5.
- Universe: the four UK nations (Table 7's nation columns; the UK column is the aggregate). Included: England, Scotland. Excluded: Wales (unchanged), Northern Ireland (rose). The decoy, Northern Ireland, has the highest agreement of all (79.0) and fails only through the two editions.
- Necessity: Doc 2 is the only source of agreement by nation for the age-of-sale question (Table 7; the headline 63.2% at L267 is all respondents, not by nation; Table 8 is organisations). Doc 3 is the only source of 2021 nation rates and Doc 1 of 2022 nation rates (searches as in q01); Doc 4 L638 says only that 2019-2021 declines "were seen across all constituent countries", Doc 2 L417 gives only the UK 12.9%. Without Doc 3 or Doc 1, NI's rise cannot be seen and the natural assumption (all rates falling) leads to 79.0. Recall: rev 0 probes of q01 misremembered NI's 2021 rate as "about 14.3" (a fall), which also gives 79.0. Probes for this question recorded below when run.
- Selected-lever checks: Match, then exclude: without the exclusion the highest share is 79.0; with it, 65.5. Who belongs where: positional pairing of the reordered lists (labels from the 2022 list) marks England, Wales and NI as falling, giving 79.0 (scratchpad aq02157_calc2.py).
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong year or edition) carrying Doc 4's 2019-2021 statement into 2021-2022, or assuming all nations fell: 79.0. Mode 2 (Linking across documents) positional pairing: 79.0. Mode 3 (Wrong kind of entity) organisations, Doc 2 Table 8 (England only 87.9, Scotland only 80.6): 87.9. All recomputed. Considered and not declared: all respondents' headline 63.2% and Table 7's UK 62.5 (no nation filter possible); including Wales as "not rising" leaves 65.5 unchanged.
- Calculation verification: Python Decimal 2026-10-08 (scratchpad aq02157_calc2.py): fell = England, Scotland; max(61.6, 65.5) = 65.5. Reasoning expressions exact in float (13 - 12.7 is 0.3000000000000007, within 1e-9).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: the page overview gives UK rates only and no Annex 1 figures. "65.5" also appears at D01 L1831 (Table 45, Wales "No" on vape prices), unrelated. Shortest complete route: both nation lists, name matching, four changes, Table 7 Agree row.
- Precision/readings: "smoking rate" is the ONS adult rate in both lists; Doc 1 L60's NI 21.3% is youth vaping and Doc 5 L88's Scotland 11% is maternal smoking at booking (2023), neither a 2021/2022 pair. "Fell in 2022" compares the 2022 rate with 2021's. "Individuals" fixes Table 7 (Table 8 is organisations; the headline mixes both). "The generational tobacco sales ban" is the age-of-sale change (born on or after 1 January 2009 never legally sold tobacco); proxy sales, product scope and warning notices are separate questions (Tables 9-14: Scotland 76.8, 65.6, 73.4), each a different measure. England's "13%" (no decimal) still shows a fall for any 12.95-13.05.
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps.
- Style/set review: 22 words, no em dashes. Shares the nation lists with q01 (rev 1), but q01 asks a projected gap and q03 a Table 7 share; neither gives the other's answer.
- Warnings answered: pending preflight.

sections.question: Among UK nations whose smoking rate fell in 2022, what was the highest share of individuals backing the generational tobacco sales ban?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source fact (Doc 3, ONS report Adult smoking habits in the UK: 2021): the adult smoking rate was 13% in England, 14.8% in Scotland, 14.1% in Wales and 13.8% in Northern Ireland.

Step 2. Source fact (Doc 1, ONS Adult smoking habits in the UK 2022): the rate was 12.7% in England, 14.1% in Wales, 14.0% in Northern Ireland and 13.9% in Scotland. This list gives the nations in a different order, so each nation is matched by name.

Step 3. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): England: 13 - 12.7 = 0.3 percentage points lower in 2022, so its rate fell.

Step 4. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Scotland: 14.8 - 13.9 = 0.9 percentage points lower in 2022, so its rate fell.

Step 5. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Wales: 14.1 - 14.1 = 0, so its rate did not fall.

Step 6. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Northern Ireland: 14.0 - 13.8 = 0.2 percentage points higher in 2022, so its rate rose and Northern Ireland is excluded.

Step 7. Source fact (Doc 2, Table 7, percentage of those responding as individuals, by where they live, on whether the age of sale should be changed so that anyone born on or after 1 January 2009 will never be legally sold tobacco products): Agree was 61.6 in England, 51.4 in Wales, 65.5 in Scotland and 79.0 in Northern Ireland.

Step 8. Calculation (from Steps 3, 4 and 7; Doc 3, Doc 1 and Doc 2): of the two nations whose rate fell, Scotland's agreement exceeds England's: 65.5 - 61.6 = 3.9 percentage points, so the highest share is Scotland's 65.5%.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong year or edition
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

### Failure mode 3
Trap: Wrong kind of entity
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

Why these are traps: Doc 4 says declines were seen across all UK nations (2019-2021); assuming that again keeps Northern Ireland, whose rate rose from 13.8% (Doc 3) to 14.0% (Doc 1), giving 79.0. Positional pairing of the reordered lists does likewise. Doc 2's Table 8 organisations give 87.9. Individuals: Scotland, 65.5%.
